question.leadin: In his pseudo-historical book 1421, Gavin Menzies claimed that an explorer from this dynasty visited the Americas before Christopher Columbus.
question.text: Name this Chinese dynasty, renowned for its blue and white porcelain, which succeeded the Yuan dynasty and preceded the Qing dynasty.
question.clue: General Wu Sangui's opening of Shanhai Pass ended this dynasty, which was crushed at the battle of Songjin.

swap.leadin: He wrote the Little Red Book and took his country on a failed Great Leap Forward.
swap.text: Name this leader who led China from 1949 until 1959 and led the Chinese Communist Party until his death in 1976.
swap.clue: He led his forces from Jiangxi to Shaanxi to escape Kuomintang persecution as part of the Long March.

question.leadin: A protest here led to Jeff Widener's iconic photograph of a man, possibly named Wang Weilin, standing in front of four tanks.
question.text: Name this Beijing square tragically cleared on the night of June 4, 1989 after Deng Xiaoping's conservative faction used their control of the military.
question.clue: In 1976, mass public displays of mourning at this site prompted disciplinary actions initiated by the Gang of Four.

swap.text: The UK turned over control of this Special Administrative Region to China in 1997, two years beforePortugal did the same with nearby Macau.
swap.clue: At that time, this polity was restored to its previous owner, who had this polity ceded to them in 1842 after the First Opium War.

question.leadin: This dynasty's capital of Kaifeng (kai-FUHNG) was sacked by the Jurchen in the Jingkang incident, forcing this dynasty to move its capital to Hangzhou (haang-JOH).
question.text: Name this dynasty, which ruled China from 960 to 1279 CᐧE. It was conquered by Kublai Khan and succeeded by the Yuan Dynasty.
question.clue: Bi Sheng worked under this dynasty, which switched lines of succession due to the Jingkang Incident.

swap.text: This man strongly opposed opium trade, which helped to spark the First Opium War. He was later blamed by the Daoguang Emperor for the conflict. His anti-opium measures in Guangdong resulted in more than 1,700 arrests.
swap.clue: This author of the "Letter of Advice to Queen Victoria," who was appointed Commissioner in Canton to help resolve the city's drug problems.

question.text: The invasion was set off by this incident, in which Japanese military personnel framed China for plotting to blow up railroad lines owned by Japan.
question.answerHtml: Mukden Incident [or September 18th incident; or Liutiaohu Incident; prompt on "Manchurian Incident"]
question.clue: The Qing dynasty ended in 1912, though their last emperor-Puyi-became the puppet ruler of Manchukuo [man-choo-kwoh] after this 1931 incident in which a bomb went off near a railway controlled by Japan.

swap.text: This name is given to the era preceding the Warring States period, during which royal authority began to decline. It takes its poetic name from a set of Annals traditionally attributed to Confucius.
swap.clue: That royal family's flight from Zongzhou to Chengzhou initiated this time period, which the rise of the states of Wu and Yue.

question.leadin: This state's ambassador Bolad convinced the foreign ruler Gaykhatu to adopt its Chao paper currency. The residents of Tabriz did not care for it, and promptly strangled Gaykhatu.
question.text: Identify this ruling dynasty that divided society into four classes like hanren and nanren. Guo Shoujing and Amir al-Din helped build its capital at Dadu.
question.answerHtml: Yuan Dynasty [prompt on "Empire of the Great Khan"]
question.clue: It ended when the Red Turban Rebellion forced Togon Temur to flee its capital of Dadu in 1368.

swap.leadin: Emperor Gaozu stopped ripping off these peoples' hats and peeing in them after Lu Jia outlined how he should rule in the New Discourses.
swap.text: Name these people who typically wore the Liang Guan crown. The phrase "fenshu kengru" describes how Qin Shi Huang would burn books and bury these people alive.
swap.answerHtml: scholars [or Confucian scholars; or literati or wénrén; or mandarins or guān; prompt on civil servants or officials or bureaucrats; prompt on elites or gentry]
swap.clue: The intensive preparation needed to become one of these people by undertaking the Gwageo meant most were also a yangban.

question.leadin: The yin privilege allowed high ranking bureaucrats to place their sons into low positions of power without having to deal with this system.
question.text: Name this system, success in which allowed scholar-bureaucrats to advance by demonstrating knowledge of wenxue. The challenging Eight-legged essay was an integral part of this system.
question.answerHtml: Chinese imperial examinations [accept equivalents like the Chinese civil service exams]

swap.leadin: When he extended his hand out to John Foster Dulles, Dulles refused to shake this person's hand.
swap.text: Name this premier under Mao Zedong who attended the 1954 Geneva Conference.
swap.clue: A ban on publicly mourning this politician led to the 1976 Tiananmen Incident, which was cleared by an order from the Gang of Four.

question.text: This Cantonese woman terrorized southern Chinese trade in the early 19th century as the commander of the Red Flag Fleet, which consisted of over 300 junks manned by over 20,000 pirates.
question.answerHtml: Ching Shih [or Mistress Ching or Zheng Shi; or Zheng Yi Sao or Cheng I Sao or Shi Yang; prompt on Ching or Shi or Zheng or Cheng; accept answers indicating the wife of Zheng Yi, since that’s a common Chinese designation for her; do not accept or prompt on “Zheng Yi” alone]
question.clue: The largest pirate fleet ever was this woman's 80,000-man strong Red Flag Fleet around the seas around Guangdong ["gwong dung"]. This woman's step son Cheung Po outlined pirates rules which included prohibitions on sexual assault.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Chinese agricultural development in the 1900s.
swap.text: Steel melting policies popularized by the Dazhai village agriculture program caused the failure of one of these projects named Banqiao ["bahn-chyao"]. Another of these projects disrupted the baiji's ecosystem.
swap.answerHtml: hydroelectric dam [or the Banqiao Dam; or the Three Gorges Dam]

question.leadin: This document was the first of a series of three similar announcements, and it included a pledge that neither party would "seek hegemony" in the Pacific region.
question.text: Identify this landmark diplomatic communique issued in 1972 from the namesake city that began the process of normalizing US-Chinese relations.
question.answerHtml: the Shanghai Communiqué [or the Joint Communiqué of the United States of America and the People’s Republic of China]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a Chinese book.
swap.text: It was written by Luo Guanzhong and details the end of the Han dynasty to the reunification over a century later.
swap.clue: A man who later imprisons Hua Tuo is defeated at the Battle of the Red Cliffs by Zhuge Liang, while Guan Yu and Zhang Fei join Liu Bei in this work's first chapter, which sees the three of them make the Oath of the Peach Garden.

question.leadin: Many courtesans were trained at a performing arts academy in this city nicknamed "the Pear Garden."
question.text: Name this city, where an imperial consort held a comic ceremony whereby she wrapped a general in a large silk diaper. This city also contains the Great Wild Goose Pagoda.
question.answerHtml: Xi’an (“shee-AHN”) [or Chang’an] (Yang Guifei wrapped An Lushan in a diaper.)
question.clue: The Silk Road had its eastern origin in this city, where Emperor Qin Shi Huangdi was buried with his Terracotta Army.

swap.text: An Lushan was assassinated by one of these people who An had made a eunuch. These people, who ruled the Liao Dynasty, founded a "black" state after a Jurchen invasion in 1124 forced them to flee to Central Asia.
swap.clue: The Goryeo Dynasty engaged in a series of wars with these Mongol barbarians. Ruled by the Liao Dynasty, they were based out of Manchuria and launched three major invasions of Korea.

question.leadin: This event was preceded by the slaying of a man blamed for the loss of Tong Pass.
question.text: Identify this July 756 incident on the way to Chengdu in which an emperor was forced by his soldiers to order an unwanted execution. The victim and her family were blamed for an ongoing rebellion.
question.answerHtml: execution of Yang Guifei [or execution of Consort Yang; or execution of Yang Yuhuan; or execution of Taizhen]

swap.leadin: This figure established the so-called "Second Zhou Dynasty"
swap.text: Name this Chinese empress whose 690-705 rule interrupted the Tang dynasty.
swap.clue: This ruler abdicated after having a pair of rivals de-limbed and drowned in wine, and rose to power after convincing Gaozong that Lady Wang had murdered his child.
